page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is an entry-tier virtual server from the High Performance lineup, offering a balance of basic compute and fast local NVMe storage. The instance features two shared vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture, backed by 4 MB of L2 cache and 16 MB of L3 cache. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per virtual core) and provides a bundled 100 GB NVMe solid-state drive along with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

Benchmark results reflect entry-level compute capability and shared-resource constraints. The Geekbench single-core score of 1167.0 falls within the average range, but the multi-core score of 2057.0 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 2729.87 place it in the lower quartile of tested cloud instances. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth is limited, measuring 11.67 GB/s for reads and 9.16 GB/s for writes, which corresponds to poor performance in memory-intensive tests such as PassMark memory (1006.83) and database operations (496.09).

Given the shared single physical core and modest memory ceiling, the server offers efficient entry-level infrastructure without enterprise tier expenses, though throughput under continuous parallel load is limited. The fast local NVMe storage compensates for low raw memory bandwidth when handling disk-bound tasks. This server fits low-traffic web serving, development environments, lightweight background workers, and microservices with modest memory requirements.
